newsitem.title: DENMARK: FORECAST-Denmark next to raise rates in Europe.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Denmark next to raise rates in Europe.

text.p: Denmark, with strong growth, falling unemployment and upward wage pressure, is likely to be the next European country to raise interest rates, says an analysis published on Friday by investment bank PaineWebber.
The bank sees the gap between Danish and other countries' short-term rates widening and advises investors to get out of near-dated Danish state paper.

"The advanced cyclical position of the Danish economy, in comparison to other continental countries, suggests that Denmark will be the first to raise rates on fundamental grounds, although any tightening is likely to remain limited," it said.
"The risk of a diverging short-term interest rate differential between Denmark and its European neighbours favours switches out of short-dated Danish government bonds," the survey added.

It expected strong consumer demand, fuelled by falling unemployment and growing real incomes and said that a further boost was likely to come from increased refinancing activity in the mortgage market.
It saw inflation -- 2.4 percent in December on an EU-harmonised basis -- as likely to rise toward the central bank's three percent ceiling during the year.
